## Flag Explanation

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-l` | List all loaded modules |
| `-v` | Verbose output — show module metadata, load timestamps, and dependency chains |

## Example Output

```
$ p7c -l -v
[14:23:07] [p7c] Loading modules from: /zenka/modules
[14:23:07] [p7c]   ✓ core.zenka (v3.2.1)    [12.4ms]    [base]
[14:23:07] [p7c]   ✓ zenka.os (v1.0.3)    [8.1ms]     [base]
[14:23:07] [p7c]   ✓ zenka.net (v2.1.0)    [15.2ms]    [zenka.os]
[14:23:07] [p7c]   ✓ zenka.log (v1.4.2)    [4.3ms]     [zenka.os]
[14:23:07] [p7c]   ✓ zenka.cache (v0.9.1)    [6.7ms]     [zenka.os, zenka.log]

Total: 5 modules loaded in 46.7ms
```

The `-v` flag is the key differentiator here — without it, you only see the module name and version; with it, you get load times, dependency resolution, and error context if a module failed to initialize.
